mainTopic: Which widow receives יבום or חליצה, why only one of two wives is handled, and רבי עקיבא's view that a child from a חלוצה's relative is a ממזר.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a משנה: if one widow may marry a כהן and the other may not, חליצה is done with the one who is already unfit. The גמרא first rereads 'four brothers' as 'four of the brothers.' It then shows that the eldest may marry all four widows only if he can support them, and that stopping at four is good advice so each wife gets her עונה. Next it asks why a יבם deals with only one of two wives. The singular 'house' in the פסוקים allows only one יבום or one חליצה. The rule that only a woman eligible for יבום can have חליצה rules out mixing the two. The repeated word 'יבמתו' shows that יבום still applies when there are two wives. רב יוסף learns from the משנה not to cause others a needless loss. A new משנה follows: רבי עקיבא and the חכמים argue over whether a child from remarrying a divorcée, a חלוצה, or a חלוצה's relative is a ממזר. After trying to change the משנה's wording, the גמרא keeps it, explaining that for רבי עקיבא the Torah calls the חלוצה 'his house.' The amud ends as רב יוסף begins listing cases where everyone agrees, a teaching that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Choosing which widow gets חליצה and which gets יבום
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by saying that if one widow is fit for כהונה and one is unfit, חליצה goes to the unfit one and יבום to the fit one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of the widows was fit and one was unfit: if he is doing חליצה, he does it with the unfit one. If he is doing יבום, he does it with the fit one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a practical rule for which widow should receive חליצה and which should receive יבום, when only one of them is fit to marry a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חליצה makes a woman forbidden to marry a כהן. So the brother should do חליצה with the woman who is already unfit, so that no new harm is done. יבום causes no such harm, so it may be done with the fit woman.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit, here meaning allowed to marry a כהן
Unfit, here meaning already forbidden to a כהן
Performs חליצה, the ceremony that releases the widow from יבום
Performs יבום, marrying his brother's widow

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general idea: when you have a choice, act so that nobody loses a status they would otherwise keep.

phrases.english: If one was fit
phrases.notes: Fit means she may still marry a כהן. A woman who has had חליצה loses that right.

phrases.english: and one was unfit,
if he is doing חליצה
he does חליצה with the unfit one,
and if he is doing יבום
he does יבום with the fit one.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: חליצה goes to the widow who is already unfit for כהונה, and יבום may go to the fit one.

steps.title: Could all four brothers have died?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's opening words, which sound as though all four brothers died.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא begins: 'Four brothers'? Could you really think that all four brothers died?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the wording at the start of the משנה. If all four brothers died, no brother would be left to do יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the משנה says four brothers who married four women died. But the משנה then talks about a surviving brother doing יבום. Both cannot be true, so the wording needs fixing.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה
Would it enter your mind? An expression that rejects an idea as impossible

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Four brothers, can that enter your mind?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the end of the משנה back to its opening words.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If all four brothers died, nobody is left to do the יבום that the משנה describes.

steps.title: Read it as 'four of the brothers'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording: the משנה means four of a larger group of brothers died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: four of the brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing how we read the משנה. It means four brothers out of a bigger family died, and at least one brother is still alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The small change from 'four brothers' to 'four of the brothers' removes the problem. There were more than four brothers, so a living brother remains to do יבום or חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say this. The גמרא is rereading the text
Of the brothers, meaning some from a larger group

phrases.english: Rather, say:
four of the brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All four brothers in the family died.
steps.terutzMaskana: Four out of a larger group of brothers died, so a brother remains for יבום.

steps.title: Do they really let him marry all four?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that the eldest may do יבום with all the widows, and asks whether he would really be allowed to do that.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'he has permission.' But would they really leave him alone to do that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'he has permission' and challenges them. It is setting up a ברייתא, coming next, that seems to say otherwise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets the eldest brother marry all four widows. The גמרא doubts that the court would just stand by and allow it. Its proof is in the following step.

keyTerms.meaning: He has permission. The choice is his
And do they leave him? Would they really let him?

phrases.english: He has permission.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: if the eldest wants to do יבום with all four widows, he may.

phrases.english: And do they leave him to do so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new quote from the משנה and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the eldest may do יבום with all four widows
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The court is supposed to steer the יבם away from a match likely to cause trouble. Marrying four women seems like exactly such a match.

steps.title: The elders must give the יבם good advice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the פסוק about the elders calling the יבם. They must do it themselves and give him advice that suits him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: 'And the elders of his city shall call him.' It must be they, not their messengers. 'And they shall speak to him' teaches that they give him advice that suits him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source behind its challenge: a ברייתא saying the זקני העיר personally guide the יבם and give him fitting advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads two parts of the פסוק. 'Shall call him' means the elders must do it personally, not through messengers. 'Shall speak to him' means they give him advice that is right for him. So the court is involved and does not just leave the יבם to decide alone.

keyTerms.meaning: The elders of his city, the court
Their messengers
Fitting, suitable advice

phrases.english: But it was taught in a ברייתא:
"And the elders of his city shall call him"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:8

phrases.english: They, and not their messengers.
"And they shall speak to him"
teaches that they offer him
advice that suits him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source that powers the challenge in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge that the court would not simply leave the יבם to marry all four
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the פסוק in דברים 25:8

steps.title: Example: do not bring fighting into your home
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives an example of fitting advice. When the ages do not match, the elders tell the יבם to marry someone like himself and avoid fighting at home.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was young and she was old, or he was old and she was young, they tell him: Why go after a young woman? Why go after an old woman? Go to someone like yourself, and do not bring fighting into your home.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains what 'fitting advice' means through an example about a big age gap. This finishes the גמרא's challenge to the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The elders steer the יבם away from a match likely to cause quarrels, even if that means choosing חליצה. Marrying four women could also bring tension, for example because supporting them all is hard. So the ברייתא seems to clash with the משנה's 'he has permission.' Step 7 answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: Go toward, turn to
Someone like you
Quarreling, fighting

steps.whatToRemember: The court actively advises the יבם and steers him away from matches likely to cause fighting. That is why the משנה's 'he has permission' to marry four widows is being challenged.
steps.confusionAlert: The age-gap example is not the case of the משנה. It is only a model of the court's role, which the גמרא applies to marrying four women.

phrases.english: That if he was young
and she was old,
or he was old and she was young,
they say to him:
What do you want with a young woman,
what do you want with an old woman?
Go to someone like yourself,
and do not bring fighting into your home.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאִם הָיָה הוּא יֶלֶד וְהִיא זְקֵנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 5 and explains what 'fitting advice' means.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge to the משנה's 'he has permission'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's example of the elders steering the יבם away from a mismatched match

steps.title: Only when he can support them all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a case where the eldest brother is able to provide for all four widows.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the משנה is needed for a case where he is able to do it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 4. The eldest may marry all the widows only when he can really support all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in steps 5 and 6 warned the elders to give the יבם advice that suits him. That does not cancel the משנה. The משנה's ruling simply applies to a man who can handle all four wives.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for... (narrows the case)
where it is possible for him

phrases.english: No, it is needed
for a case where it is possible for him.
phrases.notes: He means he has the money and strength to support all four women.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 4 through 6 by narrowing the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Marrying all four widows goes against the elders' advice to the יבם.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of a man who is able to support all of them.

steps.title: Then why stop at four?
steps.stepSummary: If what matters is being able to support them, the same should hold for more than four widows.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even many more should also be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. If ability is all that counts, why does the משנה speak of four?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 7 made ability the deciding factor. But ability has nothing to do with the number four. So the number in the משנה now looks random.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
many, a lot

phrases.english: If so,
then even many more as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The number four in the משנה, given the answer of step 7
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If being able to support them is the only condition, any number should be allowed. Then there is no reason to mention four.

steps.title: Good advice: no more than four
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches good advice. Up to four wives is fine, but no more, so that each wife gets her marital time at least once a month.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us good advice: four, yes; more, no. That way he can give each one her time once a month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the number four is good advice, not a strict limit. With four wives, each one still gets her marital rights at least once a month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number four is not about money. It is about the husband's duty of עונה, his marital time with each wife. With more than four, he could not reach each wife even once a month.

keyTerms.meaning: good advice
it teaches us
more
a wife's right to marital time with her husband

steps.whatToRemember: A man may marry many wives if he can support them, but the advice is to stop at four so that each wife gets her עונה at least once a month.

phrases.english: It teaches us good advice:
four, yes; more, no,
so that each one will get her marital time once a month.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 and closes the discussion of the four widows.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The number four in the משנה has no meaning.
steps.terutzMaskana: Four is advice, based on the husband's duty of עונה to each wife.

steps.title: Why not יבום with both wives?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, about a man with two wives, and asks why the יבם cannot do יבום with both of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: one who was married to two women, and so on. So let him do יבום with both of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. A brother died childless and left two wives, and the משנה says the יבם deals with only one of them. The גמרא asks why he cannot marry both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that יבום or חליצה with one wife frees the other wife, her צרה. The גמרא asks why one is enough. It wants to know why he could not simply marry both widows.

keyTerms.meaning: and so on (the rest of the quote)
to both of them
a co-wife (another wife of the same husband)

phrases.english: One who was married, and so on.
phrases.notes: The משנה is speaking of a man married to two women who died without children.

phrases.english: But let him do יבום with both of them!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁהָיָה נָשׂוּי וְכוּ׳. וּנְיַיבֵּם לְתַרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the יבם deals with only one of the two wives
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Step 9 showed that a יבם may marry several widows. So why should he not marry both wives here?

steps.title: He builds only one house
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן learns from the פסוק "his brother's house," written in the singular, that a יבם builds only one house, not two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the פסוק says "who does not build his brother's house." He builds one house, and not two houses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from a פסוק. The Torah says "house" in the singular, so a יבם may marry only one wife of his brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "house" here means a wife of the dead brother. Since the פסוק says one house, he does יבום with only one wife. That is why the משנה has him deal with just one of them.

keyTerms.meaning: one house (here, one wife of the brother)
builds

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר קְרָא: ״אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִבְנֶה אֶת בֵּית אָחִיו״,
phrases.english: The verse says: "who does not build his brother's house"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:9

phrases.english: he builds one house,
and he does not build two houses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 from a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He could do יבום with both wives.
steps.terutzMaskana: The singular "house" limits יבום to one wife of the brother.

steps.title: Why not חליצה with both?
steps.stepSummary: If he cannot do יבום with both, the גמרא asks why he cannot do חליצה with both.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let him do חליצה with both of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the next option. Maybe the יבם can at least do חליצה with both wives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in step 11 was about building a house, which is יבום. It said nothing about חליצה. So maybe חליצה with both wives is still allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: so let him do חליצה

phrases.english: So let him do חליצה with both of them?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests a different option, since step 11 covered only יבום.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that he does חליצה with only one wife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The limit to one house was learned only about יבום, so חליצה with both may still be allowed.

steps.title: He does חליצה for only one house
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא בר טוביה learns from the פסוק "the house of him whose shoe was removed" that חליצה is also done for only one house.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא בר טוביה said: the פסוק says "the house of him whose shoe was removed." He does חליצה for one house, and not for two houses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from another פסוק. The word "house" appears in the singular again, this time about חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like step 11. The singular "house" in the חליצה פסוק limits חליצה to one wife. So חליצה with both wives is ruled out as well.

keyTerms.meaning: the one whose shoe was removed
does חליצה

phrases.english: Mar Zutra bar Toviya said:
The verse says: "the house of him whose shoe was removed"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:10

phrases.english: he does חליצה for one house,
and he does not do חליצה for two houses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 with a פסוק that works like the one in step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He could do חליצה with both wives.
steps.terutzMaskana: The singular "house" limits חליצה to one wife as well.

steps.title: Why not יבום with one and חליצה with the other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests mixing the two: יבום with one wife and חליצה with the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let him do יבום with one and חליצה with the other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one more option. Two of the same is not allowed, so maybe one of each is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 11 and 13 each ruled out doing the same act twice. They did not rule out one יבום plus one חליצה. That way, each act would happen only once.

keyTerms.meaning: to one (of them)

phrases.english: So let him do יבום with one
and do חליצה with the other!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for a gap left by steps 11 and 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that he deals with only one wife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each פסוק only stopped two of the same act. A mix of one יבום and one חליצה seems to slip past both limits.

steps.title: חליצה only where יבום is possible
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק "if he does not want" shows that חליצה applies only where the man could have done יבום if he wanted to. After יבום with one wife, he can no longer do יבום with the other, so he cannot do חליצה with her either.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "if he does not want." That means if he did want, he could do יבום. Anyone who can go up for יבום can go up for חליצה. Anyone who cannot go up for יבום cannot go up for חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from a פסוק and sets out a general rule. חליצה is only for a woman the man could have married through יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says חליצה happens when the man "does not want" יבום. That means he had the choice to want it. Once he did יבום with one wife, the second wife is not open to יבום, so she is not open to חליצה either.

keyTerms.meaning: if he does not want
but if he did want
one who can go up for יבום (is eligible)

steps.whatToRemember: The rule is: only a woman who could have had יבום can have חליצה. So when a brother leaves two wives, the יבם deals with just one of them, and that frees the other.
steps.confusionAlert: The rule does not say that every woman who could have יבום must have חליצה. It says חליצה only works where יבום would have been possible. That is why, after יבום with one wife, the other wife is left out of חליצה as well.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, כל העולה ליבום עולה לחליצה, is a key principle. It ties חליצה to the possibility of יבום, and it is used in many other cases.

phrases.english: The verse says: "If he does not want"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:7

phrases.english: which means that if he wanted, he would do יבום.
Anyone who can go up for יבום can go up for חליצה,

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין עוֹלֶה לְיִיבּוּם — אֵין עוֹלֶה לַחֲלִיצָה.
phrases.english: and anyone who cannot go up for יבום cannot go up for חליצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: ״אִם לֹא יַחְפּוֹץ״, הָא חָפֵץ — יְיַבֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 and closes the questions about the two wives.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Learning from a פסוק, which gives a general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He could do יבום with one wife and חליצה with the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: חליצה is only for a woman who could have had יבום. After יבום with one wife, the other cannot have יבום, so she cannot have חליצה either.

steps.title: A second reason: a house half built and half released
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives another reason the יבם cannot do יבום with one wife and חליצה with the other: people will say the brother's house was partly built and partly released.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another reason: so that people should not say, 'This house is partly built through יבום and partly released through חליצה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second reason to the answer from step 15 about why the יבם cannot mix יבום and חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 used the פסוק 'if he does not want.' Now the גמרא adds a practical worry: a mixed result would look like one house handled in two opposite ways. The next lines will explain why that appearance is a real problem.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; an additional reason
House; the dead brother's family line
Built; done through יבום
Released through חליצה

phrases.english: And furthermore, so that people should not say:
a house that is partly built
phrases.notes: 'Built' means through יבום, like the פסוק about building a brother's house.

phrases.english: and partly released through חליצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second reason to the answer given in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Additional reason based on how things look to people
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One could mix יבום with one wife and חליצה with the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Mixing is not allowed, partly because the house would look half built and half released.

steps.title: So what if people say it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second reason: what harm is there if people say the house is half built and half released?
steps.simpleTranslation: So let them say it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the reason just given, asking why people's talk should matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A worry about appearances needs a real halachic danger behind it. The גמרא wants to know what actual problem this saying would cause.

keyTerms.meaning: And let them say; so what if they say it?

phrases.english: And let them say it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason 'so that people should not say the house is half built and half released'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Talk alone is not a problem unless it leads to a real violation.

steps.title: The real danger: חליצה first, then יבום
steps.stepSummary: Doing יבום first and then חליצה would be fine, but if mixing were allowed, someone might do חליצה first and then יבום, which breaks the rule of 'לא יבנה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did יבום first and then חליצה, that would indeed be fine. But perhaps he will do חליצה first and then יבום, and then he violates 'he does not build.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the real problem behind the worry about appearances.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order matters. Once a man does חליצה, the פסוק calls him one who 'does not build' his brother's house, so he may no longer do יבום with any of the wives. If mixing were allowed, people might do it in the wrong order and come to this violation.

keyTerms.meaning: Does יבום
Does חליצה
And then; afterward
'He does not build'; after חליצה he may not do יבום

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that חליצה closes the door on יבום for the whole house, not only for the woman who received חליצה.

phrases.english: If he does יבום and then does חליצה
indeed, that would be fine.
But perhaps he does חליצה and then does יבום,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording; some versions don't have it.

phrases.english: and he ends up violating 'he does not build.'
phrases.notes: דברים 25:9

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דִּמְיַיבֵּם וַהֲדַר חָלֵיץ הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the hidden real danger behind the concern
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The concern was just about what people would say.
steps.terutzMaskana: The concern is that people would do חליצה before יבום and violate 'לא יבנה.'
steps.whatToRemember: Mixing is not allowed: the פסוק 'if he does not want' limits it, and allowing it could lead to חליצה before יבום, which is forbidden.

steps.title: Maybe two wives means no יבום at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that perhaps the מצוות יבום applies only when the dead brother left one wife, and not when he left two.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say this: when there is one wife, the מצוות יבום applies; when there are two wives, the מצוות יבום does not apply at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new, bigger challenge: maybe with two wives there is no יבום at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא assumed the יבם does יבום or חליצה with one of the two wives. Since the פסוקים speak of a single house and a single woman, maybe two wives remove the מצווה completely.

keyTerms.meaning: But say; why not suggest
One
Two
The מצווה of marrying a dead brother's wife

phrases.english: But say: when there is one wife
the מצוות יבום applies,
when there are two wives
the מצוות יבום does not apply!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: כִּי אִיכָּא חֲדָא תִּתְקַיֵּים מִצְוַת יִבּוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the 'one house' readings of steps 11 and 13 further, suggesting they rule out יבום entirely when there are two wives.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that יבום applies when the dead brother left two wives
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פסוקים speak only of one house and one woman, maybe a case with two wives is outside the מצווה altogether.

steps.title: Proof from צרת ערוה that two wives can do יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that the Torah's ban on a צרת ערוה would be pointless if two wives never had יבום anyway, so יבום must apply with two wives.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need the law that the Torah forbids the צרה of an ערוה? Now, if even two ordinary wives cannot have חליצה or יבום, is it needed to say this about the צרה of an ערוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to reject the suggestion of step 19 by bringing a proof from the law of צרת ערוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צרת ערוה always means at least two wives: the ערוה and her co-wife. If two wives never have יבום, the Torah would not need a special rule forbidding the צרה. Since the Torah did make that rule, it seems two wives normally can have יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: A co-wife of a woman who is a forbidden relative to the יבם
The Merciful One; the Torah
Why do I need it?
Is it necessary to say?

phrases.english: If so, the צרה of an ערוה
which the Torah forbade, why do I need it?
Now, about two ordinary wives you say
that they are not eligible for חליצה and יבום
is it necessary to say it about the צרה of an ערוה?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, צָרַת עֶרְוָה דְּאָסַר רַחֲמָנָא לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to disprove the suggestion of step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That the מצוות יבום does apply when the dead brother left two wives
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Torah's ban on a צרת ערוה, which would be unnecessary if two wives never had יבום

steps.title: The proof fails: the ערוה might have been ignored
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the צרת ערוה law is still needed, because we might have thought the ערוה does not count, leaving the צרה as if she were the only wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not? It is still needed. You might have thought: the ערוה stands outside and does not count, so her צרה should do יבום as the only wife. So the Torah teaches us that the צרה is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if two wives never have יבום, a צרת ערוה is special. Since the ערוה herself can never do יבום, we might have treated her as not there, making the צרה like a single wife. The Torah's ban teaches that she is still forbidden, so the ban is not wasted and proves nothing about two ordinary wives.

keyTerms.meaning: Why not?
It was needed
You might have thought
Stands outside; is not counted
It teaches us

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not say two wives have no יבום. It only shows that the צרת ערוה proof does not settle the question either way.

phrases.english: Why not? It is still needed,
because you might have thought:
the ערוה stands outside the picture,
so her צרה should do יבום,
so it teaches us that she is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 20, so the question of step 19 needs a different answer. Step 22 gives it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from צרת ערוה, not the larger question
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The צרת ערוה law has its own purpose: to stop us from ignoring the ערוה and treating the צרה as a lone wife.

steps.title: The double word 'his יבמה' includes a case of two wives
steps.stepSummary: After rejecting the proof from צרת ערוה, the גמרא brings a new source: the Torah repeats the word 'יבמתו,' and this extra word widens יבום to include a dead brother who left more than one wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the source is that the Torah says 'his יבמה' and again 'his יבמה.' The repetition comes to include more cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The previous proof was pushed away, so the גמרא now gives a new, final source that יבום applies even with two wives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21 the גמרא showed that the צרת ערוה law could be needed even if two wives never have יבום. So that proof fell apart. Now the גמרא says the Torah repeats the word 'יבמתו,' and an extra word like this 'widens' the law to include a dead brother with more than one wife.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; the earlier idea is dropped and a new one replaces it
His יבמה, the widow of his brother who needs יבום
Included or widened; an extra word adds more cases to the law

steps.whatToRemember: The source that יבום applies even when the dead brother left two wives is the repeated word 'יבמתו,' not the law of צרת ערוה.

phrases.english: Rather: 'his yevama,' 'his yevama' — the Torah included more cases.
phrases.notes: The word shows up more than once in the יבום section, דברים 25:5-7.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof that was rejected in step 21 with a new source from the wording of the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That the מצוה of יבום applies even when the dead brother left two wives.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The repeated word 'יבמתו' in the פסוקים of יבום, read as including more cases.

steps.title: Do not spill water that others need
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case where one wife is fit to marry a כהן, and רב יוסף says this teaches a general lesson: do not throw away something you don't need if others need it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if one of the wives was fit (to marry a כהן), the brother should not do חליצה with her. רב יוסף said: here רבי taught that a person should not pour out the water of his pit when others need it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, where one wife is fit for a כהן. רב יוסף draws a general life lesson from that ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חליצה makes a woman forbidden to marry a כהן. If the brother does חליצה with the fit wife, he takes away her chance to marry a כהן for no reason, since he could do it with the other wife instead. רב יוסף compares this to dumping water you don't need while others are thirsty for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit; here, a woman still allowed to marry a כֹּהֵן
רַבִּי (רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא) taught this in the מִשְׁנָה
His pit or cistern for storing water

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns a technical rule of חליצה into a general lesson: do not cause others a needless loss, even when it costs you nothing to avoid it.

phrases.english: If one was fit.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה: one wife can still marry a כהן, so don't do חליצה with her.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, כָּאן שָׁנָה רַבִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Here Rabbi taught:
A person should not pour out the water of his pit,
when others need it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, כָּאן שָׁנָה רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of where יבום with two wives comes from, and comments on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the משנה's rule not to do חליצה with the wife who is fit for a כהן, we learn that one should not cause a needless loss to others.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: these forbidden marriages produce a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: someone who remarries his divorcée, marries his חלוצה, or marries a relative of his חלוצה must divorce her, and רבי עקיבא says the child is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A man who takes back his divorced wife, or marries the woman he did חליצה with, or marries a relative of that woman, must divorce her, and the child is a ממזר. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists three forbidden marriages and gives רבי עקיבא's view that a child from them is a ממזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three marriages are forbidden, so the man has to divorce her. רבי עקיבא goes further and says the child born from such a marriage is a ממזר, even though these sins do not carry כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, our מִשְׁנָה
One who takes back his divorced wife
The woman he did חֲלִיצָה with
He must send her away, meaning divorce her
A child born from certain forbidden relationships, who may not marry into the Jewish people

steps.confusionAlert: Not every forbidden marriage makes a ממזר. רבי עקיבא's opinion here is wider than the חכמים' opinion in the next step.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who takes back his divorcée,
phrases.notes: This means after she married someone else in between, which the Torah forbids (דברים 24:4).

phrases.english: and one who marries his ḥalutza,
and one who marries a relative of his ḥalutza —
he must divorce her, and the child is a mamzer;
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a brand-new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Remarrying one's divorcée, marrying one's חלוצה, or marrying her relative requires divorce, and according to רבי עקיבא the child is a ממזר.

steps.title: The חכמים: no ממזר, except with a relative of a divorcée
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי עקיבא and say the child is not a ממזר. But they agree that if a man marries a relative of his divorcée, the child is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: the child is not a ממזר. But they agree that if a man marries a relative of his divorced wife, the child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the חכמים' opinion, which argues with רבי עקיבא, and then points out one case where they agree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים hold that these marriages, though forbidden, do not make the child a ממזר. A relative of one's divorcée is different. That is one of the עריות, which carry כרת, so there everyone agrees the child is a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Sages say; the opposing opinion
And they agree; the point where both sides agree
A relative of his divorced wife, such as her sister or mother

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: a child from these forbidden marriages is a ממזר. חכמים: not a ממזר, except for a relative of one's divorcée, where all agree he is a ממזר.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'a relative of his חלוצה' (they argue) with 'a relative of his divorcée' (they agree the child is a ממזר).

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: The child is not a mamzer.
But they agree about one who marries a relative of his divorcée —
that the child is a mamzer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to רבי עקיבא's ruling in step 24 and marks the case where both sides agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, the child from these marriages is not a ממזר, except a child from marrying a relative of one's divorcée.

steps.title: Can a rabbinic prohibition make a child a ממזר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא's ruling about a חלוצה's relative, citing ריש לקיש that a חלוצה's sister is forbidden only by rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי עקיבא really hold that a man who marries a relative of his חלוצה has a child who is a ממזר? But ריש לקיש said that in this משנה, רבי taught that a divorcée's sister is forbidden by Torah law, while a חלוצה's sister is forbidden only by rabbinic law!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by attacking one case in the משנה: how can a child from a union forbidden only by the רבנן be a ממזר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ממזר comes only from a Torah-level forbidden union. ריש לקיש says a חלוצה's sister is forbidden only מדברי סופרים. So רבי עקיבא's ruling that the child is a ממזר seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman released from יבום through the חליצה ceremony
A relative of the woman he did חליצה with
Forbidden by Torah law
Forbidden by rabbinic law
But didn't he say? (opens a contradiction)

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not whether a חלוצה's sister is forbidden; she is. The problem is that the prohibition is only rabbinic, and a rabbinic prohibition cannot produce a ממזר.

phrases.english: GEMARA: And does Rabbi Akiva hold
that one who marries a relative of his ḥalutza,
the child is a mamzer?
But didn't Reish Lakish say:
Here Rebbi taught:
a divorcée's sister is forbidden by Torah law,
a ḥalutza's sister is forbidden by rabbinic law!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה quoted in steps 24-25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's ruling that the child of a חלוצה's relative is a ממזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ממזר requires a Torah-level prohibition, but ריש לקיש says a חלוצה's sister is forbidden only rabbinically.

steps.title: Change the משנה's wording to a divorcée's relative
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the משנה: read it as 'a relative of his גרושה,' not 'a relative of his חלוצה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach instead: a relative of his divorcée.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by adjusting the words of the משנה so that רבי עקיבא's ruling is about a divorcée's relative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A divorcée's sister is forbidden by Torah law, so a ממזר can come from that union. By changing one word, רבי עקיבא's ruling fits ריש לקיש's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A relative of his divorced wife

phrases.english: Teach: a relative of his divorcée.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is changing the wording here, so read the משנה as saying 'גרושתו' instead of 'חלוצתו.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the text of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה said רבי עקיבא calls the child of a חלוצה's relative a ממזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה really says a relative of his גרושה, which is a Torah prohibition.

steps.title: The word 'they agree' supports the fix
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה says the חכמים 'agree' about a divorcée's relative, which only makes sense if רבי עקיבא already mentioned that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also logical, since the end of the משנה teaches: 'But they agree that one who marries a relative of his divorcée has a ממזר child.' If you say רבי עקיבא spoke about that case, that is why it says 'they agree.' But if you say he did not speak about it, what does 'they agree' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the corrected wording from the phrase 'ומודים' at the end of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'They agree' means the חכמים accept something רבי עקיבא already said. If רבי עקיבא had talked only about a חלוצה's relative, there would be nothing to agree to. So רבי עקיבא must have spoken about a divorcée's relative.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is logical (introduces support)
The end part of the משנה
And they agree
He was talking about it

phrases.english: So too it is logical,
since the end of the משנה teaches:
"But they agree about one who marries a relative of his divorcée
that the child is a mamzer."
It works well if you say he was talking about it;
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי עקיבא, and 'it' is the case of a divorcée's relative.

phrases.english: that is why it teaches "they agree."

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לָא אַיְירִי בַּהּ
phrases.english: But if you say he was not talking about it,
what is "they agree"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the textual fix of step 27.
steps.raayaObject: The corrected wording: רבי עקיבא spoke about a divorcée's relative
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'ומודים' in the סיפא of the משנה

steps.title: Maybe 'they agree' teaches a ממזר from כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests 'they agree' could be a fresh teaching: a ממזר can come from a union punished by כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps this teaches us that a ממזר can come from those unions punished by כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof: maybe 'they agree' does not refer back to רבי עקיבא, but teaches a new rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A divorcée's sister is a כרת prohibition. So maybe the סיפא is simply teaching that even a כרת union produces a ממזר, and says nothing about what רבי עקיבא discussed.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
This is what it teaches us
Unions punished by כרת

phrases.english: But perhaps this teaches us
that there is a mamzer from unions punished by karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof of step 28.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'ומודים' might be a new teaching about כרת, not agreement to רבי עקיבא's case.

steps.title: That rule is already taught in a later משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion, since a later משנה already rules that a ממזר comes from כרת unions.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is already taught later: Who is a ממזר? Any close relative forbidden under 'he shall not come,' says רבי עקיבא. רבי שמעון התימני says: any union punished by כרת at the hands of Heaven. And the הלכה follows his words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its proof: the משנה here would not need to teach the כרת rule, because a later משנה teaches it openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later משנה already rules like רבי שמעון התימני that כרת unions make a ממזר. Teaching it again here would be repetitive. So 'they agree' must still be referring back to רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Later on (in a later משנה)
A close blood relative
Being cut off, a punishment from Heaven
And the הלכה follows his view

phrases.english: That is already taught later on:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה on 49a.

phrases.english: Who is a mamzer?
Any close relative
who is under "he shall not come" —
the words of Rabbi Akiva.
Rabbi Shimon HaTimni says:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁחַיָּיבִין עָלָיו כָּרֵת בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם
phrases.english: any union for which one is liable to karet at the hands of Heaven.
And the halacha follows his words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the objection of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the suggested teaching would be repetitive
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ומודים' teaches that a כרת union produces a ממזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: That rule is already stated in the משנה on 49a, so it is not needed here.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה is stated anonymously to show the halacha
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה here repeats the כרת rule without a name to show it is the accepted halacha.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps the תנא stated it here without a name, following רבי שמעון התימני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back again: maybe the repetition has a purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה stated with no name usually signals the הלכה. So the סיפא might be repeating רבי שמעון התימני's view anonymously to show it is the הלכה, and still not refer to רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא states it to us anonymously

phrases.english: But perhaps the tanna stated it to us without a name
phrases.notes: When a משנה gives a view without naming anyone, that usually shows it is the הלכה.

phrases.english: following Rabbi Shimon HaTimni.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 30.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the כרת teaching would be repetitive
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Repeating a view anonymously has a purpose: to fix it as halacha.

steps.title: Then why pick a divorcée's relative?
steps.stepSummary: If the goal were to teach the כרת rule anonymously, the משנה would list כרת cases in general, not specifically a divorcée's relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let it teach the other כרת unions. Why do I need a relative of his divorcée?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the latest suggestion by asking why the משנה would choose this one case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An anonymous ruling for רבי שמעון התימני would mention כרת unions generally. Picking a divorcée's relative shows the משנה is responding to a case already raised by רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let it teach
Why do I need it?

phrases.english: If so, let it teach
the other unions punished by karet;
why do I need a relative of his divorcée?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the objection of step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the specific choice of case only fits the original reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא anonymously restates רבי שמעון התימני.
steps.terutzMaskana: Then it would list כרת cases in general; the specific case shows it refers back to רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: It seems רבי עקיבא spoke about a divorcée's relative
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי עקיבא's ruling was about a relative of a divorcée, supporting the corrected wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that he was talking about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof: for now, 'they agree' seems to show that רבי עקיבא spoke about a divorcée's relative. The next step challenges this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both objections in steps 29 and 31 were answered. So at this stage 'ומודים' seems to refer back to רבי עקיבא, which would support reading the משנה as 'a relative of his גרושה.' Step 34 pushes back on this, and step 35 ends up keeping the original wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, learn from this

steps.whatToRemember: This is only a temporary conclusion. The proof from 'ומודים' is pushed away in step 34, and in step 35 the גמרא keeps the original wording: for רבי עקיבא, a חלוצה's relative is forbidden by the Torah.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this: he was talking about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the back-and-forth that began in step 28.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For now it appears that רבי עקיבא's ruling concerns a divorcée's relative. Step 34 rejects this, and the original wording is kept in step 35.

steps.title: Maybe the divorcée's relative was only listed alongside similar cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 33. Perhaps רבי עקיבא never ruled about a divorcée's relative at all. The משנה may have listed that case only because it resembles the other cases he did teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe רבי עקיבא was not really talking about a divorcée's relative at all. He taught about a man who remarries his divorcée, a man who marries his חלוצה, and a man who marries a relative of his חלוצה. Since those cases were taught, the משנה also mentioned a relative of one's divorcée, simply because it is a similar case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the conclusion it just reached. It says the mention of 'a relative of his divorcée' does not prove anything about רבי עקיבא's own ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 28 through 33 argued that the משנה's special mention of a divorcée's relative shows רבי עקיבא ruled on that case. That would support changing the wording. Here the גמרא answers that the case could have been included just to match the list of similar cases. If so, the proof falls away, and so does the support for changing the wording.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps (introduces another way to read the source)
He was not talking about it
Since it taught (one case, it also taught a similar one)
A relative of his divorced wife

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a divorcée's relative is permitted. It is only saying the משנה's wording does not prove what רבי עקיבא held about that case.

phrases.english: But perhaps he really was not talking about it at all,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and since he taught 'one who remarries his divorcée'
and 'one who marries his halutza, or a relative of his halutza' —
it also taught 'a relative of his divorcée.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 33 for changing the wording.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference that רבי עקיבא's ruling must have been about a divorcée's relative.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case could have been listed only because it resembles the cases next to it (אַיְּידֵי), so its presence proves nothing.

steps.title: Keep the original wording: for רבי עקיבא a חלוצה's relative is a Torah prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא stops trying to change the wording. It answers the original question directly: according to רבי עקיבא, the relative of one's חלוצה is forbidden by the Torah, so the child is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we keep the משנה as it is. According to רבי עקיבא, a child from a relative of one's חלוצה is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its original question, how a ממזר can come from a union with a חלוצה's relative. It answers that רבי עקיבא really does hold the child is a ממזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original problem was that marrying a חלוצה's relative seemed to be only a rabbinic prohibition, and a ממזר should not come from that. Now the גמרא accepts the plain wording and assumes רבי עקיבא treats this prohibition as coming from the Torah. That clears the way for a ממזר. The source for this comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier approach and gives a new one)
A relative of the woman who did חליצה with him
A child born from a forbidden union who may not marry into the regular community

phrases.english: Rather: a relative of his halutza —
according to Rabbi Akiva, the child is a mamzer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: קְרוֹבַת חֲלוּצָתוֹ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הָוֵי מַמְזֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the attempt to change the wording failed in step 34, the גמרא answers the original question with the text left as it is.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the plain wording and explaining it: the prohibition is from the Torah according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A חלוצה's relative is only rabbinically forbidden, so the משנה's wording had to be changed.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי עקיבא the relative of one's חלוצה is forbidden by the Torah, so the child is a ממזר.

steps.title: The פסוק calls the חלוצה connection 'his house'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives רבי עקיבא's source. The Torah calls the חלוצה's connection to him 'the house of the one whose shoe was removed.' This means she counts like a wife, so her relatives are forbidden to him by the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This is רבי עקיבא's reason. The פסוק says 'the house of the one whose shoe was removed.' The Torah calls her 'his house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source from the פסוק that supports the answer in step 35.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Torah language, 'house' can mean a wife. By calling the חלוצה 'his house,' the פסוק treats her as connected to him like a wife, even though they only did חליצה. So her relatives become forbidden to him the way a wife's relatives are, and that is a Torah prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the reason
'The house of the one whose shoe was removed' (דברים 25:10)
His house, meaning his wife or family connection
The פסוק called it

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, the Torah treats a חלוצה like a wife ('his house'). Because of that, her relatives are forbidden to him by the Torah, and a child from such a union is a ממזר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the status of a חלוצה's relative from a rabbinic prohibition to a Torah one, according to רבי עקיבא. It solves the whole problem that sent the גמרא into the long discussion about changing the wording.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
This is the reason of Rabbi Akiva:
For the verse says: 'The house of the one whose shoe was removed,'
phrases.notes: דברים 25:10

phrases.english: the verse called it 'his house.'
phrases.notes: 'His house' here means she is treated like his wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source from the פסוק for the claim in step 35.
steps.raayaObject: That for רבי עקיבא a חלוצה's relative is forbidden by the Torah.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 25:10, 'בית חלוץ הנעל': the חלוצה is called 'his house.'

steps.title: רב יוסף begins: all agree about one who remarries his divorcée
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף, quoting רבי שמעון בר רבי, starts a new teaching. He lists cases where everyone agrees, beginning with a man who remarries his divorcée. The rest of the teaching comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said in the name of רבי שמעון בר רבי: Everyone agrees about a man who remarries his divorcée…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new statement that lists cases where all opinions agree. This line sets up what follows; the ruling itself continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about where רבי עקיבא disagrees with the חכמים. רב יוסף now marks off cases with no disagreement, starting with one who remarries his divorcée. What exactly everyone agrees on is spelled out in the coming lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
One who takes back his divorced wife

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rabbi Shimon bar Rabbi said:
All agree in the case of one who remarries his divorcée,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the explanation of רבי עקיבא's view, a new teaching begins that marks off cases with no disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening of a list of cases everyone agrees on, starting with one who remarries his divorcée. The ruling is completed in the following text.
